summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 2 diabetes, chronic abdominal pain, gastroparesis, GERD, and recurrent UTIs was admitted with persistent urinary frequency and new-onset left lower quadrant and flank pain different from her usual symptoms. She had leukocytosis and a positive urine culture showing Klebsiella pneumoniae, confirming a complicated UTI. She received IV Zosyn and had a PICC line placed for outpatient antibiotic completion. Diarrhea developed during treatment but C. difficile testing was negative. Her pain was managed with tramadol, Lyrica, and other home medications. She tolerated oral intake well by discharge. Due to the need for extended IV antibiotics, she was discharged to a skilled nursing facility. Her diabetes, hypertension, depression, and anxiety were managed with home medications throughout the stay.
